ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: "outside the eon." The Chan corpus uses it as a productive modifier and location in sayings and verse: "spring light beyond the eon" (劫外春光), "the spring beyond the eon returns and the ten thousand things wither" (劫外春回萬物枯), and "the true lineage beyond the eon" (劫外真宗).
EvidenceBody: It is paired explicitly with the time before buddhas and patriarchs were born: "before buddhas and patriarchs were born, outside the empty eon" (佛祖未生空劫外). It also enters public address as a demand to "take responsibility beyond the eon" (於劫外承當), contrasted in the same question with meeting now (而今相見, "meeting at present"). The corpus thus bends chronological language into a recurrent Chan register for the sayings, activity, spring, and lineage it places outside or before measured epochs.
